text:
tara: Quick alert - matmul microbuild (quant-kernel v5.2.2-rc1) started hitting OOMs on tiny-batch jobs in canary slice t-19 around 03:40 UTC. Putting the roll on hold.
sam: Acknowledged. Do we have logs / heap traces?
tara: paste: `gs://redwood/logs/microbuilds/6833334444/oom.log` shows repeated cudaMalloc failures; looks like a workspace size regression.
deploybot: Auto note: rollout paused for slice t-19. To pin: `deploybot pin --slice t-19 --runtime runtime-quant:v5.2.1 --until 2026-03-21T12:00Z`
infra-bot: Suggest check: kernel ABI drift? Run `kubectl exec` on a canary to capture driver vs kernel symbols.
amy: I pulled a node dump, driver matches expected (nvml 525.*). The change was an extra temp buffer allocation in matmul path for quant-ls.
sam: Can we hotfix by toggling the new allocation behind a flag? If yes, build a quick patch `v5.2.2-rc1-hotpatch` and smoke.
tara: I can try a conditional compile to skip temp buffer for small seqlen; will trigger a microbuild. Anyone object to a hotpatch today?
kevin: No objections. But we should define rollback criteria and communication. Propose: immediate rollback if OOMs > 0.2% of requests across the slice for 10m or any paging errors.
sam: Good call. Also update release notes: short note about hotpatch and that customers might see transient higher latency during fix. I'll open a PR.
deploybot: Staging build queued: runtime-quant:v5.2.2-hotpatch (job id jb-4422). smoke-checks enabled.
infra-bot: Staging smoke expected in ~8m. Will post results.
tara: Staging smoke failed with 2 OOMs on synthetic tiny-batch - reproduces. I reverted the temp buffer and kicked new build `v5.2.2-hotpatch2`.
kevin: If hotpatch2 passes, we can rollout to t-19 at 10% with tight telemetry gating (eviction/oom/error). Keep pin on v5.2.1 until then.
amy: Pin created for t-19 -> runtime-quant:v5.2.1 until 2026-03-21T12:00Z. (pin_id: p-98420)
sam: PR: https://git.redwood/release-notes/pulls/415 - added hotpatch note and rollback triggers.
tara: Hotpatch2 smoke passed: 0 OOMs in 15m test. Requesting gradual canary push to 5% with 2m evaluation windows.
eops-bot: (typo correction) infra-bot will schedule gradual push when you run `deploybot traffic-shift`.
sam: Running traffic shift: `deploybot traffic-shift --slice t-19 --pct 5 --method gradual --eval 2m --watch alert:kernel.oom > 0 -> rollback`
deploybot: Traffic shift accepted. Rolling to 5% over 3m. Monitoring alerts enabled.
kevin: I'll monitor dashboard. If any anomaly, we'll immediately unwind and escalate.
amy: Noted. I'll prepare a short sync note for #incidents and update release_notes draft.
tara: Thanks all. If hotpatch2 holds for 30m at 5% we can increase to 25% and then unpin after 4h.
sam: Agreed. Recording rollback criteria again in PR and release notes.
kevin: Great. Keep comms in this thread. :thumbsup:
